title: Honest labels, true costs and a price that pays you
course_title: Candle Making: Safe Production of Container, Pillar and Event Candles

say: Honest labels, true costs and a price that pays you.
This is the video for module 4 of Candle Making: Packaging, Pricing and Your Candle Business.
Your label is where a customer decides to trust you. Put your brand, product name and scent on the front.

panel.heading: What goes on your candle label

say: Give the net weight of the wax from your test pour, not the weight of the jar.

panel.heading: What goes on your candle label

say: Describe the wax honestly. Only say 100% soy if it really is.

panel.heading: What goes on your candle label

say: Give a burn time from your own timed test, never copied from another brand.

panel.heading: What goes on your candle label

say: Add your batch code and phone number, and the safety text: never leave a burning candle unattended, keep it 30 cm from anything that can burn, trim the wick to about 6 mm, and put it out with a snuffer, never water.

panel.heading: What goes on your candle label

say: For example, Halima takes two cured candles from batch HK-07.

say: She burns them in sessions of a few hours while she stays at home, writing the start and stop time each time, and trimming the wick before each session.

say: She takes the lower result and rounds down, so her label says about 16 hours. Every customer gets at least what she promises.

say: Match the packaging to the buyer. A gift buyer wants a box with paper filling, the ribbon on the outside of the box, and a care card.

say: Churches want plain pillars or tealights packed in dozens. Hotels want a simple clean jar and steady quality.
Candles soften in heat, so store stock in a cool shaded room, and pack jars upright with padding.

say: Many makers copy other people's prices and find out months later they were working for free. So cost every batch from your own receipts. These naira figures are example prices only.

say: Halima's wax costs 9,072 naira and her fragrance 4,080 naira.

say: With wicks, jars, dye, labels, gift boxes and gas, all her materials come to 27,452 naira.

say: Then she adds her labour: 4 hours at 1,000 naira. If you leave out your own time, your price will be too low to grow.

card.note: Example figures only. Use your own receipts.

say: The batch total is 31,452 naira. She keeps 1 candle for burn testing, so 11 are for sale. That is about 2,859 naira per candle. Any price below that loses money.

say: Profit margin is the share of the selling price that is profit.
To get a 40 percent margin, divide the cost by 0.60. That gives about 4,765 naira.
Halima rounds up to a clean 4,800 naira.
Her profit is 1,941 naira per candle.
A gift shop asks for 25 percent off.
The price drops to 3,600 naira, and her profit to just 741.
That can be worth it for a large regular order, but not for three candles.
So set a minimum order for wholesale.

panel.heading: From cost to price
panel.rule: Know your floor before you agree any discount.

say: Before you release goods, check that the money is in your own account, in your own bank, Opay or Moniepoint app.
Fake alerts are a common scam, so do not trust a screenshot or an SMS sent by the buyer.
Take a deposit for custom orders, and keep a simple sales record.

panel.heading: Before you release any candles
items: Check your own bank or payment app
Never trust a screenshot or SMS alert
Deposit first for custom event orders
Record date, buyer, item, amount, how paid

say: To remember.
Keep your label honest and tested.
Cost the whole batch, including packaging, gas, your labour and your test candles.
Divide by 1 minus your margin, then round.
And release goods only after the money is in your own account.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Label net weight, honest wax, tested burn time
Use the lower burn time, rounded down
Cost the full batch, including your labour
Price = cost divided by (1 minus margin)
Release goods only when you see the money

say: Now design your label and test your burn time.
Then cost one batch from your real receipts, work out retail and wholesale prices, and post your price list in your WhatsApp Business catalogue.
